text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

You are a man, the appointee is a man, and the panel was all men — sex bias against you is close to incoherent here. Raising it would weaken an otherwise strong case by making you look like you're reaching.

Your real case is the merit comparison. On the published criteria you appear better qualified for the leadership role: a master's in educational leadership versus "courses," plus five years actually doing the deputy's job. His edge is only classroom years.

Focus there, and on the unanswered request. Send a written follow-up citing your earlier request, asking for the reasons and the assessment of each candidate against the advertised criteria, with a deadline. Note the panel's composition only if it later becomes relevant to process.
